scope: 3.3.4. Why did transfer learning enable accurate membrane fouling prediction in the target plant?

matched: SHAP and LOFO identify model-relevant variables rather than causal mechanisms requiring independent physicochemical evidence
At FT = 0, attribution dominated by EPSc and moderate performance (R2 = 0.41) indicates base model EPSc-centered structure partially applicable
Elevated EPSc (49.6 mg/L) promotes high-water retention, poor dewaterability, and compressible high-resistance fouling layer consistent with CST (49.45 s) and specific CST (4.36 s/(g/L))
EPSc represents a shared, stably informative fouling matrix characteristic across plants
At FT = 40%, performance improves to R2 = 0.89 and EPSp rises to second most important feature
Target EPS EEM spectrum shows dominant aromatic protein-like peak consistent with source plants

Hypothesis of EPSp importance due to Fe-enriched influent supported by two Fe-dosing stages (9 and 26 mg/L): sludge-associated Fe increases 45 to 101 mg/g-MLVSS and EPSp increases 47.96 to 62.30 mg/g-MLVSS

Higher EPS protein enhances hydrophobicity and floc aggregation, promoting adhesion and cake densification consistent with target sludge viscosity (50.03 mPa·s) and specific viscosity (9.46 mPa·s/(g/L))
Two-step CIP confirms Fe-related EPS response and retained fouling layer: citric acid releases total Fe (0.62 to 43.02 mg/L); NaClO releases TOC (5.19 to 43.22 mg/L) and total Fe (1.85 to 11.16 mg/L)
Lower SCOD than TCOD (93 vs 271 mg/L) confirms dominant fouling layer is sludge-bound organic matrix with Fe constituents rather than dissolved organics alone

Decline in SMPp attribution indicates less emphasis on soluble proteins during target adaptation; SMP EEM aromatic protein overlaps with effluent EEM (Ex/Em ≈ 220–250 / 300–460 nm) indicating partial permeation through membrane
LSTM fine-tuning preserves transferable EPSc, recalibrates target-specific EPSp under Fe-enriched conditions, and de-emphasizes non-retained SMPp
